text:
Alex: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak in canary, KV cache cross-request reuse for short prefixes dropped noticeably. p50 token gen +8ms on our chat workload. anyone else see this?
Maria: saw an alert, thought it was noise. can you paste the flame graph? :eyes:
Alex: pasted a tiny flame snapshot: flame link -> https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/5999990000 (not public)
Alex: numbers: baseline: p50=28ms, p99=120ms; canary: p50=36ms, p99=128ms. cache hit-rate for prefix keys dropped from 72% -> 39% on the 1-5 token prefix cohort.
Sam: hmm. did the key hashing or key normalization change? we have a recent change that adds sequence-length bucket into the cache key for better eviction packing.
Alex: that change landed in the kernel path that also altered micro-batching boundaries. suspect mismatch: same logical prefix now maps to slightly different key because of the new bucket tag.
Jordan: if it's a key-shape churn issue we should consider a compat layer that treats the old and new key forms as aliases for a short grace period. but that has memory/TTL implications.
Sam: alternative: add a tiny lease/ownership flag on entries so sessions can claim an entry as sticky for X ms. entries with lease still eligible for reuse by others after `lease_grace` to avoid fragmentation.
Maria: can you sketch the lease API? short is best.
Sam: proposal: `KVLease{owner_id, expires_at, shared_count}`. when a request reads a prefix, it attempts `acquireLease(prefix, owner=N, ttl=50ms)`. if succeeds, mark sticky; if fails, fallback to shared read. eviction respects `expires_at` and a soft-evict margin. implement as in-memory metadata + tiny atomic CAS.
Alex: sounds promising. two concerns: 1) extra CAS ops on hot path may add latency, 2) we need to avoid lease thrash under high concurrency (many clients fighting for same prefix).
Jordan: for (1) microbench suggested CAS latency is ~150ns on our machines — should be ok if piggybacked on existing hashtable op. for (2) we can use randomized backoff and opportunistic reads (i.e., if acquire fails, still read existing KV without blocking).
Maria: also consider `tenant_salt` vs `session_id` in the key. current key = sha1(tenant + session + prefix). if session varies per request we lose reuse. maybe use `session_group` that maps many sessions to a shared reuse group for short lived UIs.
Alex: good call. that would recover reuse for ephemeral frontend sessions. but need telemetry to ensure we don't violate isolation assumptions.
Sam: we should add a perf test: reproduce harness that simulates 10k cross-session short prefix lookups, measure hit-rate and p50 with: (A) current, (B) session_group, (C) lease+session_group, (D) alias-compat fallback.
Jordan: i'll add a small flame/trace probe in the kernel path and turn on `kv_lease` feature flag. want to run on a single canary rack first.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out `kernel-canary-17` to rack-5 at 2025-11-08T14:03Z — monitored: small mem bump + slight latency regression, auto-alert created.
Alex: action items: Jordan -> enable `kv_lease` flag (canary rack); Sam -> implement minimal lease CAS and backoff; Maria -> add telemetry for key-shape churn and session_group experiment; Alex -> run the perf harness and push numbers.
Maria: can we also log sample keys (hashed) when hit-rate drops so we can see churn without leaking content?
Sam: yes, sample dump with count-limited, scrubbed tenant ids.
Alex: thanks all. low-risk plan and clear rollback path. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
